faqs.q: How does puppy class socialise my puppy safely, and is it just play or training too?
faqs.a: It's both. Puppies get the opportunity to meet and play with other pups off lead in our fenced fields, under the watchful eye of Gaynor and her assistants, whose specialist knowledge of dog body language lets them prevent any over-exuberance. Alongside the play, Gaynor teaches you how to help your puppy soften its play bites, walk on a lead, accept handling, give up valued items and greet people politely, and you'll start sit, down and recall in a fun way with a clicker.

faqs.q: Will puppy class help with my puppy's nipping and play biting?
faqs.a: Yes. Teaching your puppy to inhibit the force of its play bites is the most important priority on the Puppy Socialisation course, so that it develops a soft mouth and you prevent what can be potentially serious problems in the future. Children are encouraged to come and take part, so the whole family can learn it together. If your puppy's biting comes with growling, guarding food or real fear, mention it when you get in touch, as Gaynor may suggest a behavioural consultation.

faqs.q: Do we have to book in to the puppy socialisation classes, or can we just turn up?
faqs.a: Yes, you'll need to book your place before attending — get in touch and Gaynor will arrange a time. There is no deposit to pay for Puppy Socialisation.

faqs.q: Can I bring my children to the puppy socialisation classes?
faqs.a: Children are encouraged to come and take part in the puppy socialisation classes, and all the family can join in.
